hero.badge: Free farming advisor for Indian farmers
hero.title: Farming advice for your field, in your language.
hero.lead: Krishi Mitra reads your soil test, ten years of local weather and India's Soil Health Card records, then tells you what to grow, how much fertilizer to use and what is wrong with a sick leaf. In Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada or English.
hero.point1: No soil test yet? We start from your district's Soil Health Card results.
hero.point2: Every answer shows why: soil match, season, weather and crop rotation.
hero.alt: Four women farmers standing between rows of young green crops in Gujarat
hero.sampleNote: Pulse after paddy adds nitrogen to the soil.

stats.districts: districts with Soil Health Card data

features.title: One helper for the whole season
features.lead: From choosing a crop before sowing to checking a spotted leaf before it spreads.

crop.d: Top 5 crops ranked by soil match, season, local weather and what you grew last season.

fertilizer.d: Urea, DAP and MOP doses from your N-P-K, organic options, and a warning when a nutrient is already high.

disease.d: Take a photo. The model names the disease and shows organic and chemical treatment, with safe-use notes.

weather.d: Heavy rain, heat, frost, strong wind and fungal-risk warnings from the 7-day forecast at your location.

chat.d: Type or speak in Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada or English. Answers keep working even when the AI is busy.

fields.d: Save soil tests and the crops you grew. See how the soil changes and get advice that avoids repeating a crop.

how.title: Three steps before sowing
how.alt: Farmers sowing groundnut behind a pair of bullocks in a red-soil field in Raichur, Karnataka
how.s1d: Search your village or PIN code, or use your phone's location. District and state fill in by themselves.
how.s2t: Add a soil test, if you have one
how.s2d: Copy N, P, K and pH from your Soil Health Card. No card? We use your district's average and tell you so.
how.s3d: See the top 5 crops for the month you plan to sow, and exactly what pushed each one up or down.

field.title: Advice built on your records, not a textbook
field.lead: Every recommendation says where its numbers came from, so you can trust it or check it.
field.c1d: Recent tests count more, and you see the yearly trend.
field.c2d: District results for 2023-24 to 2025-26 when you have no test.
field.c3d: Normal temperature, humidity and rain for your sowing month.
field.c4d: What you grew before, and what farms nearby grow in the same season.
field.alt: A green moong bean crop growing across a wide field in Hoshangabad, Madhya Pradesh

languages.title: Ask the way you would ask a neighbour
languages.lead: Write or speak your question. Krishi Mitra picks the right tool, runs the models and answers in simple sentences.

leaf.title: A photo is enough to start
leaf.lead: Photograph one affected leaf in daylight. You get the likely disease, how sure the model is, and what to do first.
leaf.alt: Tomato leaves with small brown spots of septoria leaf spot
leaf.p2: Chemical doses from the label, with a safety note
leaf.p3: Not sure? It asks for a clearer photo instead of guessing

cta.title: Start with one field. It takes two minutes.
cta.lead: Free to use. Sign up with your phone number or email.

footer.tagline: Smart farming advice in your language. A final-year B.Tech project.
footer.disclaimer: Advice is guidance only. Before spraying or applying fertilizer, follow the product label, wear gloves and a mask, and confirm with your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra or soil testing lab.
